compounds.name: Oxymetholone
compounds.description: An oral anabolic androgen studied in anemia and selected wasting conditions.
compounds.mechanism: Androgenic signaling influences erythropoiesis and protein metabolism; anabolic and androgenic actions are not fully separable.
compounds.findings: A randomized dialysis trial reported changes in body composition and insulin resistance, with liver-enzyme elevations in two treated patients.
compounds.limits: Disease-specific findings do not establish long-term safety or benefits in healthy people. A 2026 liver-injury case involved concurrent testosterone and unverified products.
compounds.kinetics: Orally active; the structural modification permitting oral use is also relevant to hepatic risk.
compounds.risks: Cholestatic liver injury is a substantial concern. The archived label also describes fluid retention and adverse lipid changes.
compounds.interactions: The archived label warns of enhanced anticoagulant effects and altered glucose-management requirements; current clinical review is necessary.

adverse.context: Human case reports; the recent report cannot definitively attribute injury to one of the co-exposures.
Observed in a small controlled hemodialysis trial; its frequency is not a general-user estimate.
Listed in historical product labeling.

unknowns: Long-term molecule-specific cardiovascular incidence in nonmedical users.
Risk added by unverified commercial formulations.

compounds.name: Methandienone
compounds.description: An oral anabolic androgen with small, historical training studies.
compounds.mechanism: Synthetic androgen signaling changes endocrine feedback and tissue metabolism; a lean-mass measurement can include fluid shifts.
compounds.findings: One small crossover trial reported increased blood pressure and apparent water-related weight gain. Another found reduced endogenous testosterone without a significant strength advantage over placebo.
compounds.limits: The trials were small, old, and inconsistent; they do not establish long-term health outcomes.
compounds.kinetics: An orally active 17α-alkylated steroid; oral activity does not imply low hepatic burden.
compounds.risks: Hypertension, fluid retention, and endocrine suppression have direct clinical observations. Hepatic concerns also arise from the 17α-alkylated class.
compounds.interactions: Dedicated interaction evidence is incomplete; liver-active medicines and anticoagulants warrant product-specific clinical assessment.

adverse.context: Observed in 13 male weightlifters in a historical crossover experiment.
Investigators identified water shifts as an important explanation for apparent anabolic changes.
Reported during the second small crossover study.
Supported by the broader 17α-alkylated steroid class; not a molecule-specific incidence estimate.

unknowns: Reliable long-term event rates.
How much apparent lean-mass change represents water rather than contractile tissue.

compounds.name: Boldenone
compounds.description: A veterinary anabolic androgen with substantial uncertainty about human harms.
compounds.mechanism: Androgen receptor activation alters endocrine feedback and androgen-responsive tissues.
compounds.findings: Animal experiments report testicular tissue damage and myocardial lesions. A 2026 female-rat study found disrupted reproductive hormones and ovarian changes.
compounds.limits: Animal injuries identify hazards, not human incidence or exposure equivalence. Controlled human safety evidence is inadequate in these sources.
compounds.kinetics: The undecylenate ester changes release and persistence; animal dosing studies do not define human exposure.
compounds.risks: Reproductive and cardiac concerns are supported by animal observations. Human quantitative risk remains unresolved.
compounds.interactions: Human interaction studies are lacking; other androgenic exposure would complicate attribution.

adverse.context: Histological and inflammatory changes in male rats.
Rat heart lesions included hypertrophy and fibrosis; this cannot quantify human risk.
A 2026 study reported ovarian and hormone alterations in female rats.

unknowns: Human incidence and reversibility of cardiac and reproductive injury.
Risks of formulation contaminants and co-exposures.

compounds.name: Drostanolone
compounds.description: An androgen formerly studied as endocrine therapy for advanced breast cancer.
compounds.mechanism: A synthetic androgen acting through androgen-sensitive biology; historical oncology use does not establish selective protection from harms.
compounds.findings: A controlled comparison in advanced breast cancer studied drostanolone alongside other hormonal agents; the evidence is historical and disease-specific.
compounds.limits: These trials do not establish contemporary nonmedical safety or superiority for body composition.
compounds.kinetics: The propionate formulation is not interchangeable with other esters or unverified products.
compounds.risks: Endocrine suppression and masculinizing effects are class concerns; reliable drostanolone-specific event rates are not established here.
compounds.interactions: Molecule-specific clinical interaction data are limited.

adverse.context: Observed in mixed-androgen user cohorts; applying it to drostanolone is a class extrapolation.
Women using mixed anabolic steroids reported voice and genital changes; no drostanolone-specific frequency is established.

unknowns: Molecule-specific long-term cardiovascular and reproductive outcomes.
Comparative safety versus other androgens.

compounds.name: Metenolone
compounds.description: An anabolic androgen with small, historical clinical reports.
compounds.mechanism: Synthetic androgen signaling can affect erythropoiesis and endocrine feedback.
compounds.findings: A 19-patient refractory-anemia series described some hematologic responses without obvious survival extension; its brief safety reporting cannot establish low risk.
compounds.limits: Small uncontrolled disease cohorts are unsuitable for declaring safety in healthy users.
compounds.kinetics: Acetate and enanthate preparations differ; clinical exposure cannot be inferred from a shared trade name.
compounds.risks: Claims that this is a harmless or nonsuppressive steroid are not supported by the cited series. Class endocrine and masculinizing hazards remain relevant.
compounds.interactions: Human interaction information is insufficient for a complete assessment.

adverse.context: A class inference from mixed-androgen cohort data, not a measured methenolone-specific rate.
A class inference from women reporting anabolic-steroid effects.

unknowns: Reliable adverse-event incidence and long-term outcomes.
Whether marketed preparations match pharmaceutical formulations.

compounds.name: Mesterolone
compounds.description: An oral androgen investigated in hypogonadism and male infertility.
compounds.mechanism: Androgen activity does not itself demonstrate improved fertility or freedom from endocrine effects.
compounds.findings: The WHO randomized infertility study did not establish a significant improvement in pregnancy or semen outcomes relative to placebo.
compounds.limits: Fertility outcomes require more than a hormone or sperm-count change. Old therapeutic findings do not establish enhancement benefits.
compounds.kinetics: The manufacturer describes extensive protein binding and metabolism, with a terminal serum half-life around 12–13 hours for the investigated product.
compounds.risks: Product information describes frequent or persistent erections and hormone-sensitive tumor concerns.
compounds.interactions: The manufacturer reports no known interactions; this is not proof that interactions are impossible.

adverse.context: Described in product safety information.
Product information contraindicates prostate cancer and describes liver-tumor warnings.

unknowns: Long-term risk in people without diagnosed androgen deficiency.
Risk in unregulated products and polypharmacy.

compounds.name: Tamoxifen
compounds.description: A SERM with established oncology uses and tissue-dependent estrogen effects.
compounds.mechanism: Estrogen receptor antagonism in breast tissue coexists with agonist effects in other tissues.
compounds.findings: Product labeling summarizes randomized breast-cancer treatment and prevention data; the clinical benefit-risk balance depends on indication.
compounds.limits: Cancer prevention and treatment outcomes cannot validate unsupervised endocrine manipulation in healthy people.
compounds.kinetics: Active metabolites and metabolic variability are clinically relevant; exposure is affected by drug interactions.
compounds.risks: Thromboembolism is important. Uterine cancer warnings apply to people with a uterus, with risk quantified in particular female prevention populations.
compounds.interactions: The label warns about coumarin anticoagulants. A clinical pharmacokinetic study found that paroxetine reduced exposure to active endoxifen; medication changes require clinical review.
compounds.query: tamoxifen AND (safety OR pharmacology OR trial)

adverse.context: Established label concern; absolute rates vary by population and indication.
Documented in female risk-reduction populations; anatomy and indication matter.
Reported in the labeled clinical safety experience.

unknowns: Risk-benefit balance for nonmedical use in otherwise healthy men.

compounds.name: Clomiphene
compounds.description: A SERM used for ovulation induction, also investigated off label in men.
compounds.mechanism: Modulates estrogen feedback and gonadotropin release; the mixture contains pharmacologically distinct isomers.
compounds.findings: The approved-label evidence concerns ovulatory dysfunction. Safety signals and their relevance vary substantially between women and men.
compounds.limits: Female ovulation-induction data cannot provide male-specific adverse-event rates.
compounds.kinetics: Isomers persist differently; total exposure cannot be summarized by a single short elimination window.
compounds.risks: Visual symptoms may persist after stopping. Ovarian enlargement and hyperstimulation are relevant only to people with ovaries.
compounds.interactions: The label notes that drug interactions have not been documented; absence of documentation is not a complete interaction assessment.

adverse.context: Blur, flashes, and persistent or possibly irreversible visual effects are described in labeling.
A potentially serious complication in ovulation induction; not a male anatomical risk.
Postmarketing reports; rates and causal certainty are not established by spontaneous reports.

unknowns: Long-term safety of chronic off-label use in men.
Incidence of persistent visual symptoms by population.

compounds.name: Enclomiphene
compounds.description: A SERM isomer investigated in secondary male hypogonadism.
compounds.mechanism: Changes estrogen feedback, increasing LH and FSH in studied men.
compounds.findings: Randomized trials increased testosterone and maintained sperm concentrations compared with testosterone gel. These are laboratory endpoints, not proof of symptom or fertility improvement.
compounds.limits: The EMA assessment found missing clinically meaningful efficacy evidence and raised thromboembolic concerns.
compounds.kinetics: Metabolite characterization and chronic safety were uncertainties in the regulatory assessment.
compounds.risks: Venous thromboembolism was a material regulatory safety concern; limited studies cannot exclude rare events.
compounds.interactions: Robust product-specific interaction characterization remains incomplete.

adverse.context: EMA identified events in treated participants and judged the overall benefit-risk evidence insufficient.
This is an evidence gap, not a demonstrated absence of harm.

unknowns: Effects on symptoms, live-birth outcomes, and long-term morbidity.
Reliable individual thrombotic risk prediction.

compounds.name: Anastrozole
compounds.description: A nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor used in hormone-sensitive breast cancer.
compounds.mechanism: Suppresses conversion of androgens to estrogens; estrogen has important skeletal and metabolic functions.
compounds.findings: The ATAC program documented cancer outcomes alongside bone loss and other adverse effects in postmenopausal women.
compounds.limits: Those trial rates do not transfer directly to young men or nonmedical use.
compounds.kinetics: Orally active; clinical effects reflect sustained enzyme inhibition as well as drug exposure.
compounds.risks: Bone loss, joint symptoms, and lipid changes matter. Cardiovascular findings depend on baseline disease and comparator.
compounds.interactions: Estrogen-containing products and tamoxifen can undermine the intended pharmacologic effect; this is not combination guidance.
compounds.query: anastrozole AND (safety OR bone OR pharmacology)

adverse.context: Observed in the ATAC bone substudy in postmenopausal breast-cancer patients.
Reported in clinical trial safety data.
Context includes tamoxifen comparison and pre-existing ischemic heart disease.

unknowns: Long-term risk-benefit of estrogen suppression in otherwise healthy men.

compounds.name: Letrozole
compounds.description: A nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor with extensive oncology trial data.
compounds.mechanism: Inhibits estrogen synthesis, affecting both tumor biology and normal estrogen-dependent tissues.
compounds.findings: Long-term adjuvant trials reported more fractures and hypercholesterolemia than selected comparators.
compounds.limits: Comparator, menopause status, follow-up, and baseline risks determine the meaning of trial rates.
compounds.kinetics: Oral exposure accumulates with repeated use; hepatic function is relevant to clinical pharmacology.
compounds.risks: Skeletal adverse effects and musculoskeletal symptoms are important, alongside lipid abnormalities.
compounds.interactions: Product information describes interactions with tamoxifen and other agents; indication-specific medication review is necessary.
compounds.query: letrozole AND (safety OR fracture OR pharmacology)

adverse.context: Observed in adjuvant breast-cancer trials; absolute risks are population-specific.
Reported more often than with tamoxifen in BIG 1-98.
Common clinical trial symptoms, not evidence of therapeutic benefit.

unknowns: Safety of nonmedical use and sustained estrogen suppression outside studied indications.

compounds.name: Exemestane
compounds.description: A steroidal aromatase inactivator studied in postmenopausal breast cancer.
compounds.mechanism: Irreversibly inactivates aromatase; steroidal structure does not make it an anabolic steroid substitute.
compounds.findings: Oncology studies demonstrate disease-specific efficacy and measurable skeletal and symptom burdens.
compounds.limits: Therapeutic oncology benefit does not establish benefit from lowering estrogen in a healthy person.
compounds.kinetics: Metabolism and exposure are affected by strong CYP3A4 induction.
compounds.risks: Bone-mineral loss, joint symptoms, fatigue, and vasomotor symptoms are established concerns.
compounds.interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inducers reduce exposure; estrogen-containing agents can interfere with action.
compounds.query: exemestane AND (safety OR bone OR pharmacology)

adverse.context: Observed during clinical use and addressed in prescribing warnings.
Reported in randomized oncology trial safety data.
Reported adverse reactions; rates depend on comparator and population.

unknowns: Long-term outcomes of nonmedical use in men.

compounds.name: Finasteride
compounds.description: A DHT-lowering medicine used in prostate enlargement and hair loss.
compounds.mechanism: Inhibits conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone; effects are tissue- and indication-dependent.
compounds.findings: Controlled trials and postmarketing surveillance support different kinds of safety evidence; spontaneous reports cannot establish event frequency.
compounds.limits: Persistent-symptom reports require attention without converting voluntary reports into a population incidence estimate.
compounds.kinetics: Pharmacologic DHT suppression and plasma elimination are different measurements.
compounds.risks: Sexual adverse effects occur in trials. Persistent sexual symptoms and mood effects appear in postmarketing labeling, with attribution limits.
compounds.interactions: The label does not identify clinically important interactions with studied drugs; this is not an exhaustive interaction guarantee. PSA interpretation changes during treatment.
compounds.query: finasteride AND (safety OR adverse OR pharmacology)

adverse.effect: Reduced libido, erectile and ejaculatory symptoms
adverse.context: Reported in controlled clinical studies.
Postmarketing reports; frequency and an independent causal contribution cannot reliably be determined from them.
Included in postmarketing labeling; these data do not establish an individual risk estimate.

unknowns: Predictors and incidence of persistent symptoms.
Independent contributions of exposure, underlying illness, and other medicines.

compounds.name: Dutasteride
compounds.description: A DHT-lowering medicine with clinical data in benign prostatic hyperplasia.
compounds.mechanism: Inhibits both major 5α-reductase isoenzymes, reducing DHT formation.
compounds.findings: Controlled trials document prostate outcomes and sexual or breast-related adverse reactions.
compounds.limits: Data in older men with prostate disease do not directly quantify risks in younger hair-loss users.
compounds.kinetics: Long persistence after repeated exposure distinguishes it from short-acting agents; strong CYP3A4 inhibition can increase exposure.
compounds.risks: Sexual and breast-related effects occur in trials; PSA lowering can complicate prostate-cancer assessment.
compounds.interactions: Chronic potent CYP3A4 inhibitors are specifically highlighted in labeling.
compounds.query: dutasteride AND (safety OR adverse OR pharmacology)

adverse.context: More commonly reported with dutasteride than placebo in BPH trials.
Reported in controlled safety data.
A pharmacologic effect that can obscure interpretation without appropriate clinical context.

unknowns: Individual persistence and recovery of sexual symptoms.
Precise risk extrapolation across indications.

compounds.name: Human chorionic gonadotropin
compounds.description: A gonadotropin used in selected fertility and endocrine conditions.
compounds.mechanism: Activates the LH receptor, stimulating gonadal steroid production; physiological consequences differ by sex and reproductive anatomy.
compounds.findings: Product information describes use in ovulation induction and selected male hypogonadal conditions.
compounds.limits: Raising gonadal hormones does not establish symptom or fertility recovery after nonmedical androgen use. A 2026 endocrine society statement found no robust evidence of improved long-term recovery from pharmacologic interventions in that setting.
compounds.kinetics: An injected glycoprotein; formulation and underlying gonadal responsiveness affect exposure-response relationships.
compounds.risks: Ovarian hyperstimulation can be severe in fertility treatment. Gynecomastia and hypersensitivity are also relevant.
compounds.interactions: Can cross-react in some gonadotropin assays, complicating interpretation of LH-related laboratory results.
compounds.query: "chorionic gonadotropin" AND (safety OR pharmacology OR trial)

adverse.context: Potentially severe in people undergoing ovarian stimulation; anatomy-specific.
Reported with hCG treatment in male patients.
Reported in product safety information.

unknowns: Long-term outcomes in nonmedical endocrine manipulation.

compounds.name: Clenbuterol
compounds.description: A β2 agonist with human toxicity evidence from poison-center studies.
compounds.mechanism: Adrenergic stimulation affects cardiovascular physiology and shifts potassium into cells.
compounds.findings: Poison-center cohorts documented tachycardia, tremor, gastrointestinal symptoms, electrolyte abnormalities, and cardiac injury signals after misuse.
compounds.limits: Poison-center series establish clinically important hazards but cannot estimate incidence among all exposed people.
compounds.kinetics: Prolonged symptoms have been reported; product claims do not reliably predict exposure or duration.
compounds.risks: Arrhythmia, marked electrolyte disturbances, and myocardial injury are important concerns.
compounds.interactions: Additional sympathomimetic exposure is a mechanistic concern, not a validated or safe combination strategy.
compounds.query: clenbuterol AND (toxicity OR safety OR pharmacology)

adverse.context: Frequently documented in poison-center reports.
Observed metabolic effects after exposure.
ECG changes, chest pain, and elevated troponin were reported; the cohorts cannot yield general incidence.

unknowns: Reliable risk prediction for a given nonmedical product.
Long-term cardiovascular outcomes among unselected users.

compounds.name: Liothyronine
compounds.description: Synthetic T3 used for specific thyroid indications, with a weight-loss boxed warning.
compounds.mechanism: Thyroid receptor activation changes transcription and metabolic demand across tissues.
compounds.findings: The 2026 label emphasizes replacement indications and adverse effects from thyroid-hormone excess.
compounds.limits: Correcting deficiency differs from inducing excess in a person with normal thyroid function; the latter is not a validated weight-management strategy.
compounds.kinetics: Oral absorption and clinical effects depend on physiology, concomitant products, and binding or metabolism interactions.
compounds.risks: Over-replacement can cause arrhythmias, ischemia, anxiety, muscle weakness, and bone loss.
compounds.interactions: Sympathomimetics can increase cardiovascular toxicity; anticoagulant and diabetes-treatment responses may also change.

adverse.context: Recognized consequences of excess thyroid-hormone exposure, especially with underlying cardiovascular disease.
Associated with over-replacement.

adverse.effect: Anxiety, insomnia, tremor, and muscle weakness
adverse.context: Clinical features of excessive thyroid-hormone effects.

unknowns: No defensible individual safety margin can be inferred for nonmedical use from replacement therapy.

compounds.name: 2,4-Dinitrophenol
compounds.description: A toxic mitochondrial uncoupler associated with severe and fatal human poisonings.
compounds.mechanism: Dissipates the proton gradient, uncoupling respiration from ATP production and releasing energy as heat.
compounds.findings: A US/UK poison-center study recorded severe toxicity and deaths. Recent clinical mitochondrial observations describe potentially self-amplifying metabolic failure.
compounds.limits: Poisoning data cannot define a safe-use window, and mechanistic interest does not establish a therapeutic role for this chemical.
compounds.kinetics: Toxicokinetics can be prolonged and unpredictable; observations from poisoning do not support a user-facing timing protocol.
compounds.risks: Hyperthermia, acidosis, tachycardia, confusion, organ failure, and death are documented.
compounds.interactions: No combination can be considered protective on the basis of these clinical reports.

adverse.context: Documented in human poisoning cohorts and cases.
Associated with fatal outcomes; case observations suggest reinforcing mitochondrial dysfunction.
Deaths are documented; case-fatality in referred poison-center samples is not a general exposure incidence.

unknowns: An individual safe exposure cannot be derived from the clinical evidence.
The proposed reinforcing mechanism remains based on limited clinical observations.
